newsitem.title: UK: Clydeport sees lower profits for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Clydeport sees lower profits for 1996.

text.p: Port and property services company Clydeport Plc said on Tuesday that adverse trading conditions in certain cargo markets would bring down its 1996 profits compared to what it was in the previous year.
In a statement, the company said it expected to pay a final dividend of three pence per share against 4.4 p per share paid in 1995.
Clydeport had reported a pre-tax profit of 5.32 million stg for the year to December 31, 1995.
The company said it had suffered temporary interruptions to the supply of imported coal from Colombia and South Africa, specially in the second half.
Clydeport's turnover has also been affected by the BSE crisis which hit the animal feed market and the continuous volatility in the global pulp market.
The company's share price fell 19 pence to 133 1/2p at 1130 GMT in a trade turnover of 37,000 shares.

The company said it expected conditions to remain difficult in certain markets into 1997. But it said it had made progress in marketing port facilities at Hunterston and was advancing the group's property development acitivities.
"Current expectations are that 1997 should see an improvement in overall trading compared with both 1995 and 1996," the company said in a statment.
